title: Stagewatch has no PlayMap link: its finder refuses t:playmap, it keeps one 'Patterns' link and labels everything Patterns
fix: Stagewatch: accept t:'playmap' in ParseBeacon (read ports.wire as well as top-level wire). Turn the single Patterns link into a list of wire playout links keyed by hello id and kind, each with its own link:<name> item, clock:<id> check and receipt routing. Add 'playmap' => 'PlayMap' to the label switch. No PlayMap change.
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:459 (isHello only for t=='patterns'); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/AppSettings.cs:146-153 (one patternsHost/Port/Token); Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:57-58,63-64,100; Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:36,81-82 (1.3 item 5); grep playmap in Stagewatch/src: only WAVE_MAPPER
statement: Stagewatch has no first-class PlayMap link. Its finder (PatternsLink.ParseBeacon, Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:459) accepts only t:"patterns", so Find in Settings never lists a PlayMap node. Following PlayMap's clips as VT, and driving its transport with `patterns end/restart/play/pause/stop/seek`, works only by typing PlayMap's host:9941 into the single Patterns link. That link has one host, port and token (AppSettings.cs:145-152; MainViewModel.Integrations.cs:16,41-42), so pointing it at PlayMap means giving up the real Patterns link. The link is then still labelled Patterns everywhere: link:patterns, playout, "Clock vs Patterns" (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:60,63-65). Stagewatch's spec has no 'playmap' node kind (docs/SHOWBUS.md:37). Its Show network shows the raw kind 'playmap' (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:100), although PlayMap's posted context does give it a real light and headline. Stagewatch can already drive PlayMap in other ways: Triggers can POST verb lines to PlayMap's /api/cmd (only when the node is open or Stagewatch is trusted, since triggers send no token), §11 approvals can carry AI-proposed PlayMap verbs, and Screens can send redirect/identify/reload to PlayMap's /ws client. None of these gives VT following or a named link with its own clock check. Fix, on Stagewatch only: accept t:"playmap" in ParseBeacon. It already reads the top-level "wire", which PlayMap sends, so reading ports.wire is optional. Add 'playmap' => 'PlayMap' to the kind switch and 'playmap' to SHOWBUS.md's kind table. Let Stagewatch run a PlayMap playout link alongside the Patterns link, either as a list keyed by hello id or as a second link, with its own link:<name> item and clock:<id> check. No PlayMap change is needed.

title: The desk mis-rates PlayMap's verbs: it keeps 64 commands, and its matcher counts '[...]' and 'A|B' as fixed words
fix: Stagewatch: raise the commands cap to >= 256 (and state it in docs/SHOWBUS.md §6). In RiskFromCommands, stop fixed words at a word that starts with '[' and treat 'A|B' words as alternatives. Add a DeskRules test that feeds PlayMap's golden context.
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowBus.cs:97,101 (Take(64)); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:225-237 (TakeWhile !'<' && !'/'); Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Engine.Tests/Fleet/Golden/context-busy.json (199 commands, read-only replay of the matcher); Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:85-89 (asks for a cap >= 256)
statement:
Stagewatch's approval desk gets the risk of many PlayMap verbs wrong. The error is fail-safe: affected verbs are shown as high, never lower.

(1) Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowBus.cs:101 keeps only the first 64 of a peer's commands. Line 102 also cuts each verb to 80 characters. 10 of PlayMap's first 64 rows are longer than that; the ADD row is 221 characters.

(2) Approvals.cs:225-237 counts every word as fixed until it reaches one that starts with '<' or contains '/'. So '[ALL]', '[<words>]', '[QUICK]' and 'ON|OFF' become fixed words that no real line contains.

Replaying the matcher over Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Engine.Tests/Fleet/Golden/context-busy.json (199 commands, 144 of them low/review) gives 114 low/review verbs rated high:
- 5 come from '[..]' words inside the kept 64 (rows 23 and 24 SHOW ARM/DISARM, 33 PREFLIGHT, 49 OUTPUT IDENTIFY, 53 BLEND SOLVE).
- 109 are every low/review row from index 64 on (MOVE, UNDO, REDO, PROJECT SAVE, LINK STAGEWATCH, TEMPO, CALIBRATION, ...).

PlayMap makes the cap worse on purpose. It lists panic, air, transport and show rows first (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Bus/ShowContext.cs:79-94), so the rows that get dropped are mostly low/review.

Where the claim is wrong:
- 'No PlayMap proposal is ever pre-ticked' is false. A step is pre-ticked when its risk is not High (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Copilot.cs:25). 30 of the 35 low/review verbs in the first 64 are rated correctly and are pre-ticked, for example PLAYLIST FOCUS/NEW/ADD/LOOP, PLAYLIST CUE, BLIND ON/OFF/DISCARD, MEDIA IMPORT/FETCH and SCAN CANCEL.
- 'A|B' causes no wrong rating inside today's 64. The only rows there with an A|B word before a placeholder are high verbs (BLACKOUT, FREEZE, LED OUTPUT). It starts to matter once the cap is raised: CONTROL ENABLE, OVERLAY, TEMPO SOURCE, SITE MAINS, DECODE POLICY, MEDIA RULE MODE, VIDEOIO SET NDI, CONTROL DMX and MACHINE SET QOS.
- Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:85-89 asks Patterns' Eye for a cap of at least 256, not Stagewatch. Stagewatch's own docs/SHOWBUS.md §6 sets no cap at all. The desk's rule that is broken is §11 at docs/SHOWBUS.md:197-198 ('Risk is the target's call').

The fix as proposed is incomplete. I simulated a cap of 256, stopping fixed words at a word starting with '[', and treating A|B words as alternatives. About 21 alternative forms are still rated high, because PlayMap joins alternative syntaxes with ' | '. Some alternatives drop the shared opening words: row 25 'SHOW SET MINGO .. | REMOTE-VIEW-ONLY ON|OFF ..', row 108 'VIDEOIO SET NDI ON|OFF | NDI-GROUPS ..', row 195 'MACHINE SET QOS HIGH|AUTO | TIMER HIGH|DEFAULT ..'. Others repeat them: row 110 'CONTROL SURFACE ADD .. | CONTROL SURFACE REMOVE <surface>', row 120 'TIMECODE SOURCE ADD .. | TIMECODE SOURCE REMOVE/RESET'. The 80-character cut also loses the later alternatives.

So the fix also needs to:
- split each verb on ' | ' into separate syntaxes, carrying the leading fixed words onto alternatives that leave them out;
- raise or drop the 80-character verb cap, or match before truncating;
- stop at '[' words and treat 'A|B' words as alternatives;
- raise the commands cap to at least 256 and state it in Stagewatch docs/SHOWBUS.md §6;
- add a DeskRules test fed with PlayMap's golden context.

title: Every Patterns assistant proposal is rated high on the desk
fix: Stagewatch: when target.id == from.id and the sending node key is bound to that id, take the proposal's own risk (the target is speaking for itself, which §11 allows). Alternatively, Patterns lists 'APPLY <id>' in its commands at 'review'. Spec §11 says which.
statement: Patterns posts every assistant proposal to the Stagewatch desk as `APPLY <localId>: <Kind> "<title>"`, aimed at itself, with a hard-coded risk "review" (AssistantPage.cs:388). Show Bus §11 says the desk ignores that field and reads the risk from the target's listed context commands (Approvals.cs:102, MainViewModel.Desk.cs:73-83). Patterns lists no APPLY verb (ShowContext.cs:157-173), so every proposal is rated "high", is not pre-ticked and reads "CHANGES THE ROOM". That covers looks, cues, lower thirds, patterns, overlays, screens, brand and show plans, even though a proposal that draws only lands in EDIT SAFE (the preview). EYE FOCUS is not affected: it is never sent through this path, and a line naming it would be rated "low" correctly. Stagewatch follows §11 as written, so the fix belongs in Patterns: add an "APPLY <id>" row (risk "review") to ShowContextBuilder.Commands. If per-kind risk is wanted, §11 would first have to be amended to let a proposer that is also the target, with its key bound to that id, state its own risk. Today the spec does not allow it.

title: Patterns never sees a stuck Stagewatch: the stuck beat is ignored
fix: Patterns: in ReceiveAsync, handle 'beat'. With live:false, set the sight's frame Live=false and do not refresh the last word; with a plain beat, refresh it. Replace the test with the real beat shape, and add one in ShowBusAppTests where FakeStagewatch sends the stuck beat.
statement:
Patterns cannot see a stuck Stagewatch. Stagewatch says it is stuck only with `{"type":"beat","live":false}` and stops sending frames (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1265-1271, 1297). Patterns' ReceiveAsync has no case for "beat" (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:525-537), and it reads `live` only inside a state frame (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/StagewatchFollow.cs:61). The held frame therefore stays Live=true. /stage, /timer and the stage timer node keep counting on from it (StagewatchFollow.cs:136), against Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:645.

The link also stays Live. That is not only because the beat refreshes the last word: Patterns' own 2 s pings (StagewatchLinkService.cs:328-354) get pongs that Stagewatch answers off the show thread (WebServer.cs:1349-1355), and each pong refreshes `_lastWordAt` (StagewatchLinkService.cs:522). Withholding the last-word refresh on the stuck beat would change nothing.

The fix: on a beat with live:false, set `_sight = _sight with { Frame = frame with { Live = false } }` and post the change, so the existing Time and Words handling shows no time. The next state frame clears it on its own. Replace the test at ShowBusTests.cs:374 with the real beat shape, and add an app test in which FakeStagewatch sends the stuck beat.

PlayMap handles the beat correctly (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:380-382). AGMessage does not, contrary to the claim. It skips the stuck beat (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:327), but pongs to its periodic pings refresh lastHeard (nodes.js:328, 353-354), so it also keeps showing the last stage view while Stagewatch is stuck. That is a separate gap of the same kind.

title: AGMessage's stage-message proposal is not valid Stagewatch grammar
fix: AGMessage: build 'message "…" <urgency> off ack' and fix server.test.js:336. Stagewatch: add a DeskRules test that the lines peers document (AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:14) parse.
evidence: AGMessage/app/server.js:703; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowState.cs:750-756,1187-1193; Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:72-78,146-155; AGMessage/app/test/server.test.js:336; correct direct form at AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:374
statement: The claim is correct as stated, with three refinements. (1) The wrong line is pinned by two AGMessage tests: server.test.js:336 and tls.test.js:141. Both need the fix, and so does docs/NODES.md:14. (2) The desk shows the proposal as high risk because Stagewatch works out risk from its own failed parse (Approvals.cs:102 and MainViewModel.Desk.cs:78). AGMessage's `risk:'review'` is ignored. (3) DeskRules already exists at ShowBusTests.cs:292, but its stub Risk never parses a line. The Stagewatch half of the fix should extend DeskRules so it runs the peers' documented lines through ShowCommandParser.TryParse after McpEndpoint.Tokenize. The AGMessage fix stands as proposed: `'message "' + text + '" ' + urgency + ' off ack'`.

title: Stagewatch's Screens commands hit peer apps: identify flashes PlayMap's projectors on air, disconnect drops every peer link
fix: Stagewatch: mark a socket as a node when it authenticates with a node key, or when it says node=<id>. Leave nodes out of Screens' 'all' and list them under Show network. PlayMap: map 'identify' to an identify on its timer surface, or journal it only, never OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL on an armed show.
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/Screens.cs:61-65; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:77-131 (Redirect :90, Disconnect :104-116 with c.Abort(), Identify :123), :1194-1196 (ScreenId from cid); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowState.cs:881-905 (no target = all); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:776-799 (:783 OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:393-404
statement:
Stagewatch lists every non-window /ws socket as a browser screen (with or without a cid; without one it gets an "anon-" id). PlayMap, Patterns and AGMessage all dial /ws as viewers (no role=control). So "all", or no target, in `screen identify|reload|disconnect|go` reaches them, and the Screens list shows them only by their page column (/playmap, /patterns, /agmessage).

What that does at each peer:
- `screen disconnect all` aborts all three links. PlayMap holds its redial for 30 s (StagewatchLink DisconnectHold). Patterns and AGMessage redial after about 0.5 s; meanwhile Patterns shows the link as Gone and its approvals as not live, and AGMessage's send-to-stage is refused.
- `screen identify` makes PlayMap run OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5 through the "stagewatch" link session, which has the Remote role:
  - Unarmed (setup or rehearsal), PlayMap overlays every output's name and number for 5 s.
  - Armed, PlayMap's Show Mode refuses the line (the Setup class is refused for Remote). It then journals the refusal and counts it in STATE.show.refused, so there is no flash on air, only a spurious refusal.
  - Patterns and AGMessage ignore identify, redirect and reload.
- `screen go all <path>` changes only PlayMap's link detail words.

Stagewatch has a ReadKey bit for sockets that authenticated with an API key, but it does not carry it into ScreenInfo or Match. So in code, peers are indistinguishable from tablets.

Fix:
- Stagewatch: mark node-key sockets as nodes (or the sockets of peers heard on the hello). Leave nodes out of "all" and list them under Show network instead.
- PlayMap: the armed case is already refused, so map identify to its timer surface or to a journal row instead of OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL even when unarmed, rather than relying on a Show Mode refusal.

title: Patterns' real outcome never completes Stagewatch's receipt or journal
fix: Stagewatch: keep the pending CommandReceipt keyed by the link's request id, and complete it (applied or refused, with Patterns' words) from the link's Receipt event. Journal on the answer instead of on send. Add a test against the fake desk with an ERR answer.
statement: For a Patterns transport command (patterns end/restart/play/pause/stop/seek, or the desk's Last 10 s button), Stagewatch writes a journal note on send ("Patterns clip paused", MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:88). That note reaches the Show Bus context's recent events and the input for the AI show summary. Stagewatch also returns its sender a final receipt with ok:true, stage "accepted" and no refs (MainViewModel.Receipts.cs:38). When Patterns (or PlayMap at :9941 through the same PatternsLink) later answers OK @id / ERR @id, only StatusLine and the link's Status change (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:65-66; PatternsLink.cs:340-371). The sender is never told the outcome, nothing in the journal is corrected, and a refusal is never journaled. So a refused VIDEO PAUSE on a stinger's clip (Patterns ShowActions.Content.cs:486) stays recorded as "Patterns clip paused" in the journal and the context, against FEATURES.md:55-57 ("accepted until Patterns confirms it"). Fix: PatternsLink.Send must expose its request id (or return a Task) and the Receipt event must carry it. Stagewatch then journals on the answer (applied, or refused with Patterns' words). It also either holds the sender's receipt open briefly for the link's answer (the Companion and HTTP paths already wait up to 3 s) or returns stage accepted with a ref and publishes the final receipt to the sender afterwards. Add a test with a fake desk that answers ERR @id.

title: Stagewatch's Patterns link is plain text and can send the pairing token in clear to a remote desk
fix: Stagewatch: send plain AUTH only when the host resolves to loopback; otherwise report 'this desk asks for no proof — update Patterns'. Later, add STARTTLS on Patterns' 9697 and PlayMap's 9941 with pins by node id.
statement:
Stagewatch's PatternsLink (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:280-284) sends plain `AUTH <token>` to any configured host once 1.5 s pass without a NONCE. It checks neither whether the host is loopback nor the 1.1 probe's result.

Against a current remote Patterns desk this leaks the token in two cases:
(a) The desk has no token set, so it sends no NONCE (ControlService.cs:363). Stagewatch sends its stored token in clear and the desk answers 'OK open'.
(b) The greeting is delayed past 1.5 s, because NONCE follows a STATE built on the desk's UI thread (ControlService.cs:357, CommandRouter.cs:905). Here the late NONCE is also ignored, because `_proofSent` is already true (PatternsLink.cs:311). The link sits unpaired until it reconnects.

Against a pre-1.1 desk, plain AUTH is the documented way to pair (REMOTE.md:242), not wasted exposure. But per §7, a remote 1.1-era client should not fall back to it silently.

The fingerprint in the hello is the web remote's certificate, and the 9697 wire has no TLS, so there is nothing for the link to pin yet. STARTTLS is optional in §10 and covers only 9697 and 9923. It is not built anywhere, and Patterns tracks it as OPEN row L55 (low).

Fix:
- Send plain AUTH only when the host resolves to loopback, or when the operator has explicitly allowed a legacy desk.
- Never send it after the `@hi PONG` probe has shown a 1.1 desk.
- Answer a NONCE that arrives after the wait with AUTH-PROOF instead of ignoring it.
- Report 'this desk asks for no token' or 'update Patterns' instead of sending the token.
- STARTTLS on 9697 is a separate, lower-priority item. Adding it on PlayMap's 9941 would go beyond §10 as written.

title: A Stagewatch window shown on Patterns would leak its address token in STATE
fix: Patterns: in WebRow and the journal, publish only scheme://host[:port] plus the window's name for addresses whose path starts with /w/ (or any address the operator marks secret), and keep the full address in a secret store. Separately, stop pushing STATE to unpaired wire peers (spec §1.4).
evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/CommandRouter.cs:294-306 (url); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ControlService.cs:358,763-774 (greeting and Broadcast to every peer); Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md doctrine ('window addresses ride in no … frame'); Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:254-256
statement:
If an operator copies a Stagewatch window address (http://<pc>:9924/w/<token>) and puts it on a Patterns web page, Patterns publishes the full address, token included, in two places in STATE. One is web.url (CommandRouter.cs:301-306). The other is residency.holds[].key, which is 'web:' plus the full address (InputKeys.cs:11-15, ResidencyService.cs:92, CommandRouter.cs:704-706).

On the TCP wire (9697), STATE goes in plain text to every connection as its greeting, before any AUTH-PROOF, and on every push (ControlService.cs:357-358, 763-773). Open wire reads are a documented Patterns decision (REMOTE.md:39-41, PLAN §103.7). Over HTTP, /api/state is gated when a token is set.

So anyone who can reach the desk's wire port can take the token. With it they can open the window past Stagewatch's viewing code and send the window's 'shown' reports, which forges its green light in the 'window:<name>' context item. Revoking the window in Stagewatch shuts the old address.

The WEB OPEN journal row does not leak the address, because it uses ShortName. No code in either app sends a window to Patterns; it happens only by an operator's paste.

Fix: Patterns should treat a page address as possibly secret in every STATE reader. It should publish scheme://host[:port] plus a label, and make sure no published input key carries the path. For a /w/ path, it should keep the full address only in the show's secret store. The broader fix, making the wire's STATE greeting and pushes need pairing, means reopening PLAN §103.7 against Show Bus §1 rule 4. It is not a bug fix on its own.

title: Opportunity: Patterns shows a Stagewatch window on an output, with an address it is given rather than typed
fix: Stagewatch: a 'window lend <window> <node id>' verb (high risk) that hands the address to that node over its authenticated /ws as {type:'window-lease',name,path}, never in /api/windows for node keys. Patterns: a verb 'WEB WINDOW <stagewatch window name> ON <screen>' that mounts a leased address as a Web source; check the certificate in ServerCertificateErrorDetected against the Stagewatch pin already held (node:<id>); keep the address secret (G09).
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:679,689 (path only for the PIN or a control key); Stagewatch/docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:99-100; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/ViewModels/MediaPage.cs:167,193 (SavedUrls.Add only on the desk); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/WebActions.cs:45-51 (WEB OPEN only re-points a mounted page); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/WebFrameSource.cs:248-272 (no ServerCertificateErrorDetected); Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:19,24 (L10 screencast, L26 no WebView2 probe)
statement:
The gap is real; this is the accurate version. Nothing hands a Stagewatch window's address to a Show Bus peer. A node key gets no path (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:679,689). A Control key would get the path, but that over-privileges a peer, and Patterns never reads /api/windows. The Show Bus context item window:<name> has no address field, and Stagewatch's PatternsLink sends only VIDEO verbs.

On the Patterns side, no wire verb mounts a new web address on a pattern, a layer, a screen's own picture or a Library tile. `LIBRARY <name>` recalls only URLs saved at the desk. `WEB OPEN <address> ON <page>` can point an already-mounted page at a window address today, for example through a line approved in Stagewatch's queue (StagewatchLinkService.cs:454-497). That is temporary (a look recall restores the pattern's own address), needs a web page already on the desk, and puts the address into a proposal and a plain log line. WebView2 has no ServerCertificateErrorDetected handler, so an https window on Stagewatch's self-signed certificate depends on Windows trusting it, although Patterns already holds a node:<id> pin it could check against.

Once an address is mounted, Stagewatch's own window commands and the "shown" report work with no further Patterns code. So the missing pieces are only these: delivering the address secretly to a named node, a Patterns verb that mounts it on a screen and keeps it, and checking the certificate against the pin.

title: Opportunity: PlayMap joins as a native Stagewatch window instead of an anonymous Screen
fix: PlayMap: 'LINK STAGEWATCH … WINDOW <token>' (the token a secret word, typed in Network > Links, redacted like the key). StagewatchLink opens the window socket, a 'window:<name>' source draws the assignment, and the node reports 'shown' after each swap. Stagewatch: no change, apart from documenting the window link for non-browser clients in docs/SHOWBUS.md.
evidence: Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:288-300 (window link); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1143-1147,1248-1261,1337,1380-1395 (WindowShown); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ScreenWindows.cs:320-348 (green only when shown rev == sent rev); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:284,431-432; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/TimerView.cs:10-15,131-150
statement:
Real opportunity, but the Stagewatch side is mis-stated. Today PlayMap joins only as a Screen. Stagewatch's `redirect` changes only PlayMap's status words, not the picture (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:37 says otherwise). PlayMap never sends `shown`, so Stagewatch cannot observe what it shows.

PlayMap could join as a window:
- Open `/ws` as window `<name>`.
- Handle the `window`, `identify`, `reload` and `revoked` messages.
- Draw clock-like content through TimerView, the holding text or image (`/api/holding/<id>` is public), black, and its own holding page on link loss.
- Report `{"type":"shown",rev,content,hold,ms,error}`, with `error` set for any page it cannot render.
- Stop dialling on `revoked`, so its IP is not locked out.

Stagewatch's Windows tab, `/api/windows` `inStep`, the `window:<name>` light and `window hold all` would then govern it with no change to their logic.

Stagewatch does need a change, though. Its window link takes the token only as `?win=` in the URL (WebServer.cs:1145, 1021), and Show Bus 1.2 §1 rule 5 and PlayMap's own link rule forbid secrets in a URL. Stagewatch should accept the window token in a header on `/ws` for non-browser nodes (Authorization: Bearer or a dedicated header), noting that today any key is dropped when `win` is present. SHOWBUS.md needs a new window-link section (it mentions windows nowhere today) covering the header and the `shown` contract. PlayMap would store the token as a secret like the key and redact it.

title: PlayMap's timer source drops what its own doc promises (watermark, holding, flash, urgency, next, playout, redirect)
fix: PlayMap: carry the parsed fields into the timer JSON, and draw the watermark always, holding (text or image), flash and urgency. Either honour redirect as a view choice or say in SHOWBUS-NODE.md that it is words only.
statement:
The gap is real. Four details make it more precise.
(1) The dropped set is bigger than the claim says. PlayMap also parses and drops Stagewatch's blackout, holdingName, cue, style and the show{} element flags. It never reads holdingFill or flashTimer at all. No code anywhere in Mapper fetches GET /api/holding/<id>, so a holding image cannot be drawn even if its id were passed on.
(2) The watermark is Stagewatch's Free-mode licence mark, "StageWatch by Ben Rohleder". Stagewatch's licensing says it shows on every output "even during blackout", and PlayMap's own parser comment says it must always be shown. A PlayMap surface fed by a Free-mode Stagewatch therefore shows the timer with no watermark.
(3) A redirect cannot pick a view in the current design. The timer source ignores its id (EngineSources.cs:178-179), TimerView takes one JSON feed per node, and _stagewatchView is read only by the STATE detail text "showing …". The NetworkHost.StagewatchView property has no caller.
(4) The papers contradict each other. SHOWBUS-NODE.md:37 and :49-50 promise view choice, urgency, flash, holding images and watermark, while COMPETITIVE.md:49 lists the Stagewatch timer source as "Designed only".
The fix is the one proposed. Carry watermark, holding, holdingFill, flash, urgency, next and blackout into the timer JSON (new fields at the end of the object). Draw the watermark always. Draw the holding image from /api/holding/<id>, or holdingName as text. Draw flash, urgency and blackout. Then either make redirect choose what the timer source draws, or have SHOWBUS-NODE.md say it is recorded in words only. The desk's StateSnapshot reader and the Assistant's StateExplainer should take the same fields.

title: PlayMap's assistant cannot use Stagewatch's approval desk
fix: PlayMap: switch the sink on when the Stagewatch link is live with Approvals and a key, with CollectApproved=false so StagewatchLink stays the one collector. Fix G02 first so its risks read correctly.
statement: PlayMap's own assistant and MCP proposals are never offered to a linked Stagewatch approval desk. AssistantService.UseApprovalDeskAsync is the only thing that sets ProposalQueue.Sink, and production code calls it only with null (DisposeAsync, AssistantService.cs:273). NetworkHost.StartStagewatch never tells the assistant that a desk with the 'approvals' cap is linked. Lines approved on Stagewatch for this node from other proposers are already collected and run by StagewatchLink (StagewatchLink.cs:471, 524-575). This is a deliberately parked owner's decision (round 2 PLAN §9 decision 7; README.md:213 says forwarding is off), not an oversight. docs/UX.md:280 wrongly says the proposals appear on Stagewatch. The fix is to wire UseApprovalDeskAsync from the Stagewatch link's lifecycle: when the link is live with Approvals and a key, pass StagewatchSinkOptions{BaseUri from the link's host and port (https when TLS, with the pinned handler), Key, SelfId, CollectApproved=false}; when the link stops, pass null. That waits on the owner confirming decision 7, and the papers (README, UX.md, CARRYOVER) need updating to match.

title: Stagewatch's own copilot and desk cannot propose a line for another app
fix: Stagewatch: add Target (NodeRef) to CopilotStep. Let the copilot plan peer lines from PeerContexts commands (risk from the target's list). Submit them to the local ProposalDesk. Add 'Propose to <peer>…' on each Show network row's right-click menu and as an MCP tool argument.
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/Copilot.cs:23; Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:29-33; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:594; Stagewatch/docs/ECOSYSTEM.md:141-149 ('cross-node approval queue in Stagewatch's copilot' still Then/Later)
statement: Stagewatch hosts the shared queue, but neither its own copilot nor its operator can put a proposal for another app into it. The copilot's plan validation (Copilot.Check, Copilot.cs:205-211) accepts only Stagewatch grammar and drops every other line. CopilotStep (Copilot.cs:23) has no target. The copilot's context (PeerFact, AiContext.cs:11) carries the peers' lights and headlines but not their command lists, which only the desk's risk lookup reads (ShowBus.cs:48-49, MainViewModel.Desk.cs:81-83). Desk.Submit is reached only from POST /api/proposals (WebServer.cs:594). An outside client with the PIN or a control, MCP or node key can propose to a peer that way, but the MCP tool run_command has no target argument and accepts only Stagewatch grammar. The Show network rows have no right-click menu. The only direct route from Stagewatch to another app is its own 'patterns' video-transport verb (ShowState.cs:670, 1031-1058), not Patterns' wire lines. There is none to PlayMap or AGMessage. Patterns, PlayMap and AGMessage all already collect and run approved lines aimed at them, so the fix is Stagewatch-only: (1) give CopilotStep a target NodeRef; (2) add each peer's commands with their risk to PeerFact in the copilot context; (3) check a step aimed at a peer against that peer's verb list instead of ShowCommandParser, using ProposalDesk.RiskFromCommands for its risk; (4) on approval, send such a step through Desk.Submit and Desk.Approve rather than Execute; (5) add 'Propose to <peer>…' to the Show network row and a target argument to MCP run_command.

title: A node key can post a context under another node's id and change that node's risk table
fix: Stagewatch: bind (or check) the key before accepting, and answer 403 'this key speaks for another node' when BindKey refuses. Add a DeskRules test.
statement:
Stagewatch's MainViewModel.AcceptPeerContext (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:65-70) stores a posted context in PeerContexts under the node.id inside the body (ShowBus.cs:67), then calls Desk.BindKey and ignores its false. So a node key bound to AGMessage gets 200 for a context posted under Patterns' (or PlayMap's) id. That context replaces the target's own entry, and also hides the context Stagewatch pulls from Patterns itself.

The attacker then proposes straight away. RiskFor (Desk.cs:81-83) labels the proposal from the forged `commands` at Submit time (Approvals.cs:102). A "BLACKOUT ON" to Patterns can therefore be shown as low/SAFE and pre-ticked instead of high and red, which breaks SHOWBUS.md:197-198. The entry stays until Patterns' next 5 s repost, at most KeepFor (30 s); the race is trivial anyway because the risk is fixed at Submit.

The operator still has to approve, and the target still runs the line through its own checks. So this is a mislabelled risk, not an auto-run. The same forgery also poisons the Eye, peers and AI context views that read PeerContexts (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:78, 91, 114, 125).

The fix: refuse with 403 "this key speaks for another node" when BindKey fails, checked before Accept. That covers node keys only. The PIN and control keys bind nothing, and with no PIN anyone on the LAN can post, so a full fix would also have to tie a context's id to the address or key it came from. The test must go through the view model's 3-arg path: the DeskRules fake uses the 2-arg overload, which never binds.

title: AGMessage never retries a failed result report, so an approved notice ends 'undelivered'
fix: AGMessage: on each 3 s tick, retry reportResult for every ranProposals entry with reported=false until it succeeds or 5 minutes pass.
statement:
AGMessage sends a result report only for proposals that the current tick's collect GET returns. Stagewatch's Collect hands each approved proposal out exactly once: it stamps `ClaimedUtc`, and later calls skip claimed proposals. So if the single POST /api/proposals/<id>/result fails, the entry stays in ranProposals with reported=false and is never retried. Five minutes after the claim, Stagewatch's Expire marks the proposal Undelivered ("AGMessage didn't report back") although the notice ran.

Fix: on every 3 s tick, independently of what approvedFor returns, retry reportResult for each ranProposals entry with reported=false. Stop on a 2xx reply or on a 409 meaning the proposal is already settled. Do not stop at 5 minutes: Stagewatch's Result accepts a report for a claimed proposal that has already gone Undelivered (Approvals.cs:155), so a late report fixes the row.

Same root cause, needs a fix on the Stagewatch side: if the collect GET's reply is lost after Stagewatch has marked the proposals claimed, AGMessage never runs them and they too end Undelivered. Retrying in AGMessage cannot fix this. Stagewatch would need to re-deliver claimed proposals that have no result yet, for example by returning them on the target's next collect, with AGMessage's ranProposals map preventing a second run.

title: AGMessage reads 'ok' from a result object; Stagewatch sends result as a string with ok and words at the top
fix: AGMessage: when result is a string, read the top-level ok. Add a test with Stagewatch's ToJson shape.
evidence: AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:165-180 (:174); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:20-31 (result string, top-level ok and words); AGMessage/app/test/tls.test.js:74,118
statement: AGMessage's readProposal (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:166-178, `ok` at :176) reads `ok` only when `result` is an object. Stagewatch's SharedProposal.ToJson (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:20-31, served by Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:35-44 and documented in Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:250) sends `result` as a string, with `ok` and `words` at the top level. So against the real desk `proposal.ok` is always null; `words` gets through the fallback. The impact today is nil: no AGMessage code reads `proposal.ok` (server.js:708, server.js:1055 and server.js:1089-1094, app.js:181-193 use only state, words and decidedBy), and state 'done'/'failed' already carries the outcome. The tests assert a shape the real desk never sends: tls.test.js:83 and :105, and server.test.js:312 (not tls.test.js:74,118). Fix: in readProposal, take a top-level boolean `ok` when `result` is not an object (and words from top-level `words`), and add a fixture with ToJson's exact shape, `{id,from,target,line,reason,risk,state,created,decided,decidedBy,result:"…",ok,words}`, to tls.test.js and server.test.js's fake desks. The value is low: it is a latent misread and test-fidelity issue, not a broken interaction.

title: AGMessage drops PlayMap's hello
fix: AGMessage: accept any kind matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16} (as Stagewatch does at RemoteSlides.cs:183-186), label playmap as PlayMap in admin-plus.js:72, and update resilience.test.js:173.
statement:
AGMessage drops every hello whose kind is not main, agent, patterns or messenger (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:33,38, fenced by AGMessage/app/test/resilience.test.js:173). PlayMap only ever announces as "playmap" (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Bus/HelloService.cs:111, Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Bus/ShowBus.cs:50), so AGMessage never discovers a PlayMap node itself. It is missing from AGMessage's own peer list on Admin > Show network, from the peers in AGMessage's own /api/context, and from the "Heard on the network" lines of the AI brief. This contradicts AGMessage/CHANGELOG.md:43 ("every kind heard") and nodes.js:5. PlayMap does show up one hop away when AGMessage is linked to a Stagewatch that hears it, because Stagewatch's context peers include every kind except agent. In that case it appears in the "Stagewatch says … it hears playmap …" line on the admin page (admin-plus.js:27) and in the "peer playmap …" lines of the AI brief (context.js showBrief). Without a Stagewatch link it is invisible.

Fix:
- Accept any kind matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16} in parseHello.
- Add playmap: 'PlayMap' to LABEL in AGMessage/app/public/admin-plus.js:72.
- Change the 'toaster' assertion in AGMessage/app/test/resilience.test.js:173 to reject a malformed kind instead of an unknown one.
- Update the nodes.js:5 header comment and AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:9.
- Optionally add playmap to the kind table in Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:39.

title: Opportunity: AGMessage reads Stagewatch's items and commands, windows included
fix: AGMessage: put Stagewatch's red and amber items (window:* among them) in showBrief and the admin page. Offer a proposal picker built from Stagewatch's commands list (target {t:'main'}), with 'window …' marked high.
statement:
AGMessage reads only the headline, light and peers from Stagewatch's Show Bus context (context.js:71-78, 103-117; server.js:860; admin-plus.js:25-27). It never reads `items` or `commands`. Its brief and admin page therefore learn about a window only when Stagewatch's headline happens to name one. That is a single lost (amber) window, and only when nothing is red and no earlier amber item outranks it (ShowContext.cs:116-117). A second lost window, a window that couldn't show its content or is switching, and a window that is holding are never seen. The research team can send directly to the stage or propose only a `message "…" <urgency> ack` line (server.js:688-705); no other verb from Stagewatch's commands, `window hold` among them, can be proposed. The fix:
- Put Stagewatch's red and amber items, `window:*` among them, into showBrief and the admin page.
- Offer a proposal picker built from Stagewatch's `commands`, with target {t:'main'}.
- Show the risk as Stagewatch's own. Stagewatch sets the risk (Approvals.cs:102, MainViewModel.Desk.cs:73-79, and Copilot.cs:228, which makes window show, hold and revoke high), so AGMessage can only display that risk, not set it.

title: Stagewatch cannot reach AGMessage's meetings
fix: Stagewatch: a Show network right-click 'Send notice to AGMessage…' that submits a desk proposal targeted at the messenger id and approves it in the same action, because the operator typed it. It can also be a trigger action (e.g. on ItemStart).
statement:
Stagewatch has no built-in way to send AGMessage a notice. AGMessage takes "notice <text>" only as a proposal on Stagewatch's desk, approved and aimed at its node id (AGMessage/app/server.js:1061-1101). Stagewatch keeps that queue (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:81-146), but only the network endpoint POST /api/proposals (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:589-595) creates entries in it.

- No Stagewatch path creates one: the desk, the Show network panel (read-only, MainWindow.xaml:692-722), the copilot (Stagewatch grammar only, Copilot.cs:23 and 210), MCP run_command (McpEndpoint.cs:131-142) and the command grammar (ShowState.cs:663-677) all lack it.
- An external client holding the PIN or a control, MCP or node key could post one by hand.
- A self-aimed HTTP trigger (Triggers.cs:131-138, with the PIN in ?pin=) could also queue one, but that is undocumented and still needs a separate approval in Copilot.
- The meeting already sees Stagewatch's clock and current item title, with the next item in a tooltip (AGMessage/app/public/app.js:288-299). It never sees free text, and Stagewatch's speaker message is not shown.

So the show caller cannot tell the meeting room "Q&A in 2 minutes" from the desk. The suggested fix stands: a right-click on a messenger row in the Show network panel, "Send notice to AGMessage…", that submits the proposal with target {t:'messenger', id: row.Id} and line 'notice <text>' and approves it as the operator in the same action. It could also be offered as a trigger action, for example on ItemStart.

title: Patterns keeps its own speaker message while following Stagewatch
fix: Patterns: while following, send STAGE MESSAGE as POST /api/message/<text>/<urgency>/off[/ack] with X-Request-Id and the node key, and show Stagewatch's receipt and ack as the STAGE MESSAGE result.
statement:
While Patterns follows a Stagewatch ("one room, one timer"), STAGE MESSAGE / STAGE CREW / STAGE CLEAR only change Patterns' own stage state (ShowActions.Stage.cs:21-24). The link never posts to Stagewatch's /api/message, even though a node key may do so (ApiKeys.cs:85, WebServer.cs:797-808). Patterns' /stage and /timer pages still draw only the desk's own pending message, beside Stagewatch's time (ControlService.Stage.cs:81-84). Stagewatch's own message is never drawn. It is serialised only as `follows.message` in /api/stage (StageService.cs:218), which no page reads, and STATE's bus row leaves it out (CommandRouter.cs:765-777). So a speaker reading Patterns' /stage sees Stagewatch's time but Patterns' message, and Stagewatch's message to that speaker is lost. messageId and messageAck are parsed (StagewatchFollow.cs:59-60) but read only by a test, so Patterns cannot show or answer Stagewatch's ack. REMOTE.md:644 records "STAGE messages stay this desk's" as intended, and the Show Bus spec (SHOWBUS.md:146) does not require Patterns to send messages, so this is a missing feature rather than a broken contract. The fix:
- While following, send STAGE MESSAGE/CREW/CLEAR to Stagewatch over HTTP as /api/message/<text>/<urgency>/<flash>[/ack] and the matching clear verb, with X-Request-Id and the node key. Report the receipt's refs.messageId as the action's result.
- Use the frame's messageId, messageAck and messageAckBy for the "seen" state.
- Draw `follows.message` on /stage and /timer, or drop the local message box, so the speaker sees one message source.

title: Windows are not in the Show Bus contract, the hello or the frames, and their URL pass contradicts §1.5
fix: Stagewatch docs/SHOWBUS.md: add §12 windows (the window:<name> item of kind screen, the window link protocol, a 'windows' cap, window addresses as capability URLs that peers keep as secrets and never publish in STATE or journals) and copy it to Patterns and AGMessage. Code: add the 'windows' cap and a compact windows block at the end of the detail frame.
statement: Windows are missing from the Show Bus contract. Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md, and its copies in Patterns and AGMessage, have no window section. They do not describe the "window:<name>" item of kind "screen", the /api/windows read, the window verbs or the /w/<token> address. The hello caps (MainViewModel.Slides.cs:36) have no "windows" cap, and the spec's caps table (SHOWBUS.md:41) is already stale. The WebSocket detail frame has no windows block, so the Companion module, which has window actions but no window feedbacks, cannot light a key on window state. Peers are not blind, though. Patterns and AGMessage already receive each window's light and state through Stagewatch's /api/context items, and its commands list the window verbs with risk high. /api/windows also answers read and node keys, without the path. Only PlayMap, which never reads Stagewatch's context, cannot follow windows. Rule §1.5 ("secrets ride in no URL") has no carve-out for browser addresses that act as passes. That covers /w/<token> and ws?win=<token>, and also the older ?view=<code>. The spec should define window addresses as view-only, revocable, rate-limited addresses that work as passes. Peers that ever receive one, for example as a browser source, keep it as a secret, out of STATE, context and journals. No peer holds one today: node keys are never given the path. The fix: add a §12 to the master spec and its copies. Add a "windows" cap and a compact windows block at the end of the detail frame for Companion feedbacks. Optionally have PlayMap read Stagewatch's context.

title: Stagewatch's context draws windows as timer->window 'hears' links and omits most window and Patterns verbs
fix: Stagewatch: emit windows as items without a timer link (or with 'feeds' from the content they show). Add the missing window verbs and patterns transport verbs to ShowContext.Commands with Copilot.Classify's risk. Keep new fields at the end.
statement:
Stagewatch adds its window items to the links list (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:62), so ShowContext.Build (ShowContext.cs:126) emits {from:"timer", to:"window:<name>", kind:"hears"} for every window, and also for clock:patterns. The direction and verb are wrong: Stagewatch controls and shows content to the window. Patterns' Eye draws these edges when both ends are among a peer's 12 drawn items (Eye.cs:810-818). AGMessage ignores Stagewatch's links and commands entirely (context.js:102-117), so it is not part of this gap.

ShowContext.Commands lists only window show/hold/revoke and "patterns end 10". It is missing window new/cue/release/identify/reload/loss/fade/rename/delete and patterns restart/play/pause/stop/seek. Copilot.Classify already gives each of these a risk. This list is advisory text only. Its sole reader is Patterns' assistant brief, which cuts it to the first 12 entries (StagewatchFollow.cs:281), so the 13th to 15th entries already drop out. Patterns' proposals always target Patterns itself (ShowBusNodes.cs:217-224), and the desk's risk comes from Copilot.Classify, not the list. So no peer can currently propose these verbs whatever the list says.

Fix:
- Give window items a links entry of their own, kind "shows" or "controls" (from "timer" or from the content they show), instead of "hears".
- Add the missing verbs as compact, grouped entries (for example "window show|cue|hold|release <window> …").
- Make sure the verbs a peer most needs fall within Patterns' 12-entry cap, by reordering or by raising Take(12) in Patterns.
Value stays low.

title: Opportunity: the Eye draws 'Patterns screen N shows Stagewatch window lobby' across apps
fix: Patterns: when a Web source was mounted from a Stagewatch window lease, add a cross-app edge screen:<n> -shows-> <stagewatch id>:window:<name> and post it in Patterns' own context links. Stagewatch: let a window item name the node and screen showing it, from the lease.
evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/Eye.cs:772-820 (:812-819 edges within one app); Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/StagewatchFollow.cs:204-227; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ScreenWindows.cs:345 (item id window:<name>)
statement:
Opportunity, which depends on G10 because no window lease exists in either repo. Today nothing ties a Patterns screen to the Stagewatch window it shows.

Patterns' Eye draws a linked Stagewatch's context as a ShowApp with up to 12 items, reds and ambers first. These can include window:<name> (kind screen). Stagewatch links each window item to its timer with timer -hears-> window:<name>. All context edges stay inside one app: Eye.cs:812-819 needs both ends in that app's item set.

Patterns can already show a /w/<token> address through its generic Web page source, but does not know the page is a Stagewatch window. Stagewatch knows only a window's viewing device and IP (WindowObserved.Device and Address, exposed in /api/windows), not which node or screen shows it, and puts neither in the context item.

Making 'Stagewatch content -> window -> Patterns screen -> projector' one chain needs three things:
1. A Show Bus §6 amendment for a link to another node's item, such as a qualified id `<node id>:<item id>`, or a per-item field like `shownBy: {node, item}`. Today a link is defined as between two of one node's things.
2. In Patterns: ShowContextBuilder.FromEye has to let that edge through (it currently drops every link touching another app's things). Eye.cs:812-819 has to resolve a qualified id to the borrowed app's item and keep that item even when the 12-item cap would cut it.
3. In Stagewatch: put the showing node and screen on the window item, from the lease, or from the Patterns' own context. Stagewatch does not read peers' links today.

Without the amendment, a Patterns-posted edge to `<stagewatch id>:window:<name>` would be filtered out by Patterns' own builder and ignored by every consumer.

title: No test holds PlayMap's posted context under Stagewatch's 64 KB limit
fix: PlayMap: a fleet test that the posted context stays <= 64 KB (trimming command 'words' first). Stagewatch: state MaxBytes in docs/SHOWBUS.md §6.
statement:
PlayMap posts its whole Show Bus context to Stagewatch's POST /api/peers/context with no byte budget (StagewatchLink.cs:501 posts ShowContext.ToJson as built, with no cap). Stagewatch's HTTP reader drops any body over 64 KB before routing and closes the connection without an answer (WebServer.cs:1613, 319-321). PlayMap would therefore stop appearing on Stagewatch silently: the exception is only debug-logged (StagewatchLink.cs:515-519) and the link still says "following Stagewatch". It would not show "make a node key" words, which come only on 401/403.

The busy golden is 43,640 bytes with 199 commands, about 21.9 KB under the limit, so round 3's roughly 20 command rows do not threaten it. The open risk is items, peers and recent, none of which has a size cap. A verb row's journal text can be its whole redacted line, up to 64 KiB, so one long line among the last 20 can push the context over the limit.

No test in either tree holds the posted context to 64 KB, and Mapper's FakeStagewatch accepts any size. No SHOWBUS.md (Stagewatch's, Patterns', AGMessage's) states a context byte limit, while PlayMap's and Patterns' readers accept 512 KB.

Fixes:
- PlayMap: a byte budget in ShowContext.ToJson (or in the link), trimming recent texts and command words first, plus a fleet test that the busy context with 20 long recent rows stays at or under 64 KB.
- The FakeStagewatch should refuse bodies over 64 KB the way Stagewatch does.
- Stagewatch: state 64 KB in SHOWBUS.md §6, and answer an oversize POST with 413 rather than closing the connection, so the sender can say why.

title: PlayMap's whole STATE may exceed the 256 KB line cap of Stagewatch's VT link
fix: PlayMap: give a 'HELLO Stagewatch' session a video-shaped STATE (top-level v, seq, id, video) or let it SUBSCRIBE a 'video' topic. Stagewatch: once G01 lands, subscribe only to what it reads. Add an interop test.
evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:40,250-256; Mapper/docs/WIRE.md ('A connection's life' item 2; STATE section); Mapper/tests/fixtures/state (52 block fixtures, ~150 KB in total)
statement: When Stagewatch's Patterns link is pointed at PlayMap (port 9941, Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:36), PlayMap sends the HELLO session its whole STATE (WireSession.cs:274, LineSessions.cs PushState). That STATE has no bound: StateWriter writes every playlist, output, projector, device and package row. Stagewatch's PatternsLink drops any line of 256 KiB or more (PatternsLink.cs:40, :274) and only increments a `Malformed` counter that nothing reads. Neither repo tests STATE size against that cap. Today the whole STATE fixture is about 9 KB compact (main.json), and PlayMap's design plans for about 50 KB (round2/design/companion.md:303), so a typical show is 5–30x below the cap. At about 2.5–3 KB per projector+output pair, only a very large node (roughly 85+ pairs, or hundreds of playlists or devices) would cross it. If it does, the VT countdown disappears 3 s later and the link's status text is left showing its last value, with no warning. The fix stays low-value: send a 'HELLO Stagewatch' session a video-shaped STATE or add a video topic, or have Stagewatch subscribe narrowly. Add an interop test that feeds PatternsLink a STATE at the cap, and show the Malformed count in Stagewatch's link status.

title: Stagewatch's hello misses loopback, and it is sent while the server is bound to loopback only
fix: Stagewatch: also send to 127.0.0.1:9928, and return no hello when the web server's bind is loopback. Add a test that the hello is sent (today's listener test builds SlidesBeacon with a null hello, Stagewatch/tests/Stagewatch.Tests/Program.cs:1860).
statement:
The Show Bus hello sender, SlidesBeacon.Send (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/RemoteSlides.cs:161-171), sends only to 255.255.255.255:9928 and swallows any SocketException. This class serves both Stagewatch's own "main" hello and the presenter-PC agent's hello (SlidesAgent.cs:69-72). Spec §2 (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:27) says "broadcast and loopback", and Patterns, PlayMap and AGMessage all add 127.0.0.1. So a same-machine Patterns or PlayMap that follows the first live main relies on the broadcast coming back to it, which is unverified, especially on a laptop with no network card.

Separately, MainViewModel.Slides.cs:21 builds the hello whenever `_web` is non-null. That includes when the operator has turned off Remote.WebBindAll, which defaults to true; the web server then binds 127.0.0.1 (WebServer.cs:212). This breaks SHOWBUS.md:44-45. Peers then dial the hello's source address with its http/ws port (Patterns StagewatchLinkService.cs:237; PlayMap StagewatchLink.cs:66-71), which the loopback-bound listener cannot accept.

Fix in SlidesBeacon or its hello:
- Also send to 127.0.0.1:9928.
- Return no hello when Settings.Remote.WebBindAll is false, matching the other three nodes.
- Add a test that a SlidesBeacon with a non-null hello is heard on a loopback listener, and one that a loopback-bound hello is suppressed. Today the only listener test passes a null hello (Program.cs:1860).

title: Measured clock offsets are thrown away; no instant-timed cue from Stagewatch
fix: PlayMap: publish links.stagewatch.clock {offsetMs, rttMs} in STATE and the context, and convert AT instants sent by a linked session by that link's offset. Stagewatch: send PLAYLIST GO … AT <its unix ms + lead> from rundown items (G29).
statement:
PlayMap measures its offset to Stagewatch (StagewatchLink.Clock) and to Patterns (PatternsLink.Clock), but only tests read either value. Neither STATE's links.stagewatch row nor the context carries it. PlayMap reads `AT <unix ms>` on its own wall clock, not on the sender's. On Stagewatch's side, the only lines it sends are untimed VIDEO verbs: VIDEO END, RESTART, PLAY, PAUSE, STOP and SEEK, through its Patterns link. Trigger payloads have no time placeholder, and HTTP triggers cannot carry PlayMap's X-PlayMap-Token. Timecode from Stagewatch over the Show Bus is not built. Stagewatch's own offset reading is used only for its CLOCKS APART light. So today an ItemStart trigger can start PlayMap only on arrival: a Command trigger running `patterns play` or `patterns restart` through the VT link pointed at PlayMap :9941, or OSC to `/playmap/line`. That start is one LAN hop late with jitter. Nothing lets both machines agree a frame-exact start instant. Two consequences for the fix:
- Stagewatch needs a new sender, because its PatternsLink only builds VIDEO lines and it holds a single Patterns link.
- Any `AT` start from an item started by the operator's GO lands the lead time after the GO.

title: Stagewatch's running order cannot cue PlayMap (or Patterns) playlist items
fix: Stagewatch: a rundown item field 'playout: <node> <playlist> [item]' and ItemStart/Standby actions that send PLAYLIST CUE on standby and PLAYLIST GO … EXPECT … on GO through the node's link, with receipts (G07) and high risk.

title: Stagewatch's HTTP triggers cannot authenticate or read receipts; PlayMap's doc says they work
fix: Stagewatch: a per-trigger secret header (DPAPI-protected, never journalled), an X-Request-Id, and reading the receipt JSON's ok and stage into the trigger status. Mapper docs: state the token or trusted-address requirement.
statement:
Stagewatch's HTTP trigger (Triggers.cs:131-139) sends no header and reports any 2xx as OK. PlayMap and Patterns differ:

PlayMap (/api/cmd and OSC 9943): an untokened caller from another machine is refused (403) unless its address is on PlayMap's trusted list or the node has no token. A default node has a token. A token in the URL is never read, so there is no secret-in-URL workaround. Adding Stagewatch's address to the trusted list is the existing route without a secret. Refusals come back as 409, so Stagewatch already shows them as failures; it only loses accepted versus applied.

Patterns (/api/cmd): there is no HTTP trusted list. Only an open desk, loopback or X-Patterns-Token gets in, and a URL token is not read. A refused command (ERR from the router, or a cue verb/STOPALL without X-Patterns-Client) comes back as HTTP 200 with {"ok":false}, so Stagewatch reports it as OK. Patterns has no stage field and takes the request id as an "@id" body prefix, not X-Request-Id. Today's route without a secret is an OSC trigger to Patterns' OSC port. It is accepted from an OSC ALLOW-listed address, or from one that proved the token on the wire in the last 12 h, which Stagewatch's own paired Patterns link does. Its refusals are not read either.

Fix:
- Stagewatch: a per-trigger header set kept in protected storage and never journalled (X-PlayMap-Token or Authorization: Bearer; X-Patterns-Token plus X-Patterns-Client); X-Request-Id for PlayMap and the "@id" prefix for Patterns; parse the reply JSON's ok (and stage for PlayMap) rather than the status code.
- Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:38: state the trusted-address or token requirement, as WIRE.md:308-320 already does.

title: PlayMap linked to a typed Stagewatch address skips TLS and the approval desk
fix: PlayMap: for a typed address, try TLS when a pin exists or /tls answers, and probe the desk once a minute as AGMessage does. Report 'paired' only after an authenticated 2xx.
statement:
PlayMap's typed-address Stagewatch link (LINK STAGEWATCH host[:port], or the same address restored from settings) is always plain ws/http with Approvals=false unless a live Stagewatch hello matches the host at the moment the link starts (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:718-736).

Because the link is rebuilt from settings straight after the hello service starts (:265-266), before any peer is heard, and OnPeer only re-picks for an empty host (:802-806), this happens on every engine restart even when the Stagewatch is on the bus.

The verb cannot ask for TLS: ParseAddress refuses '/', so https:// fails, and there is no fingerprint argument. The consequences:
- Approved proposals targeted at PlayMap are never collected (StagewatchLink.cs:471) and become Undelivered after 60 s (Stagewatch Approvals.cs:44, :185).
- With Require HTTPS on, the plain WebSocket gets 403 (Stagewatch WebServer.cs:327), which PlayMap mislabels as "check the Stagewatch key" (StagewatchLink.cs:256-259).
- links.stagewatch.paired is just Status==Live (NetworkHost.cs:315). Stagewatch upgrades /ws even for a wrong or revoked key when no viewing code is set (WebServer.cs:1154-1170), so paired=true does not show the key works. Only the detail text carries a context-POST 401/403.

Fix (PlayMap only):
- Re-resolve a typed address against the hello when a matching Stagewatch is heard.
- Accept an https:// or fingerprint form, or probe /tls, for typed addresses.
- Probe the desk (GET /api/proposals?from=<id>) once a minute, as AGMessage does.
- Name a 403 'requires wss' rather than a key problem.
- Report paired only after an authenticated 2xx.

title: Fixed cids: two Patterns desks or two AGMessages share one Stagewatch Screen id
fix: Patterns and AGMessage: use the node id as cid (padded to 6-32 characters), or let Stagewatch take nodes out of Screens (G06).
statement: Patterns always dials `cid=patterns` (StagewatchLinkService.cs:276) and AGMessage always dials `cid=agmessage` (nodes.js:317). Stagewatch uses that cid as the ScreenId (WebServer.cs:1195) and groups by it (WebServer.cs:78). So two Patterns desks, or two AGMessages, on one Stagewatch show up as one Screens row with "+1 tab". That row has one stored name (ScreenNames[id]) and shows only the earliest socket's page, device and address. A Stagewatch Disconnect aborts both installs' sockets, and both redial at once because neither handles the "disconnect" frame. Identify, redirect and reload frames are ignored by both apps whatever the cid; only PlayMap handles them. PlayMap already sends its node id (StagewatchLink.cs:283-284), with a "playmap-" prefix when the id is not 6-32 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Fix: Patterns and AGMessage send their Show Bus node id as the cid (AGMessage has one in its hello, nodes.js:73), made valid for Screens.ValidId, or Stagewatch lists Show Bus nodes apart from Screens.

title: Patterns' context commands are too few for anyone to propose display or VT-stop lines
fix: Patterns: add VIDEO STOP (high), the LIBRARY/SCREEN PVW and take lines and the window verb from G10, each with its risk. Keep the order and add the new rows at the end.
statement:
Patterns' Show Bus context (ShowContext.cs:157-173) lists 14 commands. It leaves out wire verbs Patterns already accepts and would run from the approval queue: VIDEO STOP (REMOTE.md:81), the WEB verbs (:154-162), LIBRARY / SCREEN n PVW LIBRARY (:190), SCREEN n PVW … (:188) and SCREEN n TAKE/CUT (:187). An approved line from another app runs through Patterns' full router (AppServices.cs:682-686), so the verbs can be proposed and will run. They are just not advertised, so an AI that reads the context does not learn them, and the Stagewatch desk shows them as unknown, high risk (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:73-84, Approvals.cs:225-237).

VIDEO STOP is a direct Stagewatch-to-Patterns transport command (PatternsLink.cs:139), not a proposal, and Stagewatch already rates it high on its own rules (Copilot.cs:224). Listing it in Patterns' context as high changes discoverability only, not risk.

"Put Stagewatch's window on screen 2" truly has no verb. Patterns has no notion of Stagewatch windows, and putting the /w/<token> address into a WEB OPEN line would leak a window address into a proposal line and journal row. That needs G10's window verb.

Today no repo's AI sends wire-line proposals to Patterns: AGMessage targets the desk itself, PlayMap itself, and Stagewatch's MCP proposes only Stagewatch commands. The fix is to add the missing verbs at the end of Patterns' Commands list with their risk, for discoverability and so they are not shown as unknown: VIDEO STOP high, SCREEN n PVW … and LIBRARY review (staged, nothing reaches air), and SCREEN n TAKE/CUT and the WEB verbs high. G10's window verb goes in once it exists.

title: Patterns' Stagewatch link can be set only on the Nodes page
fix: Patterns: add a 'STAGEWATCH LINK <host[:port]>|AUTO|OFF' verb (the key typed on the desk only, as a secret), with STATE, menu and module entries.
statement: Patterns' Stagewatch link (Control.Stagewatch: Enabled, Host, ApiKey, FollowStage) and the Round 88 certificate ACCEPT can be changed on a running desk or node only from the Nodes page (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Views/Sections/NodesSection.axaml:102-120). No wire verb, OSC address, Companion action, right-click menu entry or assistant line can change them; the link can only be pre-set by writing patterns.settings.json before launch. Readers are already served: STATE's bus.stagewatch row, the module's stagewatch_* variables, the Eye and the assistant's brief all read the link. So the gap breaks the standing brief's setter side (menus and desk in step, Companion and external control, rapid rig construction), not the "every reader" doctrine. Neither docs/OPEN.md nor PLAN §105.8 records it. Fix: add a 'STAGEWATCH LINK <host[:port]>|AUTO|OFF' verb, a FOLLOW ON|OFF form and an ACCEPT form. The key stays desk-typed only, as a secret, because the wire is fail-closed and carries no secrets. Add a matching right-click entry on the Show Bus peer and the Eye's Stagewatch node, a Companion action and an assistant-proposable line. The reply and STATE's bus.stagewatch.on should say the result.

title: Patterns does not know PlayMap; PlayMap's doc claims Patterns' device links pair by proof
fix: Mapper docs: correct the claim. Patterns: proof pairing on Lines devices, a 'playmap' kind with 'add as device', and reading a heard node's CONTEXT with the commands cap raised to 256.
statement: Patterns has no PlayMap code. A heard PlayMap hello is drawn only as a generic "Playmap" app, with no context and no "add as device" offer: Patterns reads a context only from its linked Stagewatch (kind "main") and from its own twin nodes, keeping at most 64 commands (ShowContext.cs:99). Patterns can drive PlayMap only through a plain Interactive Lines device at host:9941. Patterns' LinesSession (DeviceProfiles.cs:167-190) has no NONCE/AUTH-PROOF handshake; the device Secret is PJLink-only. So that link works only when PlayMap has no token, or when Patterns' address (not PlayMap's) is on PlayMap's TrustedAddresses (Pairing.cs:113-115, WIRE.md:72,87-88). Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md drifts from PlayMap's own code and WIRE.md in two places. Lines 72-73, in the §5 "Proposed for Show Bus 1.3" item, wrongly say Patterns' device links already speak NONCE/AUTH-PROOF. Line 40 says to add PlayMap's address to the trusted list, when it should be Patterns' address on PlayMap's list. Proof pairing between the two exists only in the PlayMap-follows-Patterns direction (LINK PATTERNS, WireClient).

title: PlayMap's Patterns link is read-only
fix: PlayMap: an option to slave a playlist to Patterns' video row (seq and positionMs), and LINK PATTERNS lines for operator-sent verbs with receipts.
statement: PlayMap's Patterns link sends no operator verbs. PatternsLink.SendAsync is called only by the link's own CONTEXT poll (PatternsLink.cs:279), and nothing in the engine sends a line to Patterns. Patterns' blackout is followed: it drives PlayMap's air through FOLLOW-BLACKOUT (NetworkHost.cs:687-700, EngineCore.cs:30). Patterns' clip clock (STATE video: positionMs, seq) only fills the STATE, context and preflight text (NetworkHost.cs:300-302, 688). No playlist can chase it, because TimecodeKind has no Patterns source (TimecodeModel.cs:5). Patterns can already fire PlayMap verbs from its cue steps through a Lines device (SHOWBUS-NODE.md:40), but PlayMap cannot send Patterns a verb or a cue with a receipt. The fix has two parts on PlayMap's side. First, a Patterns chase source for the existing playlist chase, re-anchoring on seq and positionMs; it is accurate only to Patterns' STATE cadence and the link's 250 ms re-anchor window, not frame-accurate. Second, LINK PATTERNS SEND lines with receipts. Frame-accurate following also needs Patterns to emit ANCHOR lines (Show Bus 1.3 item 6, SHOWBUS-NODE.md:83-84), which Patterns does not do today.

title: AGMessage and Patterns never read each other's context
fix: Patterns: read the context of heard nodes with the 'context' cap (an agn_ token typed on the Nodes page). Or, simpler: AGMessage's context reaches Patterns through Stagewatch's peers, and the docs say so.
statement: Neither AGMessage nor Patterns reads the other's GET /api/context. Patterns fetches context only from its linked Stagewatch (StagewatchLinkService.cs:350). AGMessage fetches only Stagewatch's (nodes.js:390). No Patterns code takes or sends AGMessage's agn_ token. This matches Show Bus §8 (a Stagewatch hub: each consumes only Stagewatch's context), so it is not a contract breach. But AGMessage's admin page (admin.html:136) and comments (server.js:298, context.js:3) tell the operator that Patterns' Eye reads AGMessage with that token, which is false. What each sees of the other: a direct UDP hello, which shows as grey 'heard' in Patterns' Eye and as 'Heard on the network' / headline 'heard' in AGMessage. When both link to and post to the same Stagewatch, each also gets the other's light and headline as a one-hop peer line in Stagewatch's context, but never the other's items, recent lines or commands. Patterns' Eye therefore cannot draw AGMessage's insides (open action prompts), and AGMessage's AI cannot see Patterns' problems beyond one headline. Fix: either make Patterns read heard peers' /api/context with a typed token, or correct AGMessage's admin text and comments to say its context reaches Patterns only as a headline through Stagewatch (spec §6 already describes one-hop peers).

title: PlayMap is not in the master Show Bus spec
fix: Stagewatch docs/SHOWBUS.md 1.3: add the 'playmap' kind, its caps, a §8 row (publishes the hello, wire 9941 STATE/CONTEXT, /api/context, posts context, collects approvals; consumes Stagewatch frames, Patterns STATE), the §6 commands cap, and the window section (G22). Copy to Patterns and AGMessage.
statement:
The master Show Bus spec (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md, 1.2) and its copies in Patterns and AGMessage never mention PlayMap:
- There is no 'playmap' kind (:37) and no §8 row (:143-148).
- The caps vocabulary (:41) lacks PlayMap's own caps (playlist, media, mapping, scan, show). It also lacks 'state' and video.clock, video.transport, video.seek and video.end, which Patterns sends as well. 'approvals' is named only in §11, not on the caps line.
- None of the seven 1.3 proposals (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:67-89) is in any copy: no command cap is stated in §6, and there is no anchor cap and no window section.
- ECOSYSTEM.md (:1, :31) names three apps and still cites Show Bus 1.1.

Beyond the documents:
- Stagewatch tolerates PlayMap only generically. Its peer list shows the raw kind (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:100). Its Patterns finder accepts only t=="patterns" (PatternsLink.cs:459). Its context reader keeps only 64 commands (ShowBus.cs:101).
- Patterns and AGMessage contain no PlayMap reference at all.

Fix: write 1.3 in the master with:
- the 'playmap' kind and every cap that is actually sent, including the dotted video caps and 'state';
- a §8 row for PlayMap. It publishes the hello, wire 9941 STATE/CONTEXT and /api/context; it posts its context and proposals and collects approvals. It consumes Stagewatch /ws frames and Patterns STATE/CONTEXT;
- the §6 command cap (at least 256), which also means raising Stagewatch's Take(64);
- the window section.

Then copy it word for word to Patterns and AGMessage, and update ECOSYSTEM.md to name PlayMap and 1.3.

title: Spec copies and code disagree on the certificate lifetime; the master names a model
fix: AGMessage: copy the master §10. Patterns: TlsIdentity.Life = 825 days, with a renewal test. Stagewatch master: use Patterns' §9 wording. A test in each tree compares its copy with the master's text.
evidence: AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:168 vs Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:166-167; AGMessage/app/lib/tls.js:12,72; Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowBusTls.cs:84; Patterns/docs/PLAN.md:11972; Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:154 vs Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md:156; Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md ('No model or tool identifiers')
statement:
G39 is real for the certificate lifetime and mis-stated for the model name.

(1) AGMessage: the copy's §10 (AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:168) says five years. The master, AGMessage's code (app/lib/tls.js:12,72) and its NODES.md:8 all say 825 days. The copy's own header says the master wins, so this is a stale doc line only.

(2) Patterns: its code makes a five-year certificate, which Apple devices refuse. This is in TlsIdentity.Life (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowBusTls.cs:84) and also in the doc comment at :77 and PLAN.md:11972. Patterns' copy says 825 days and Stagewatch's own code uses 825 (NodeCertificate.cs:66). This is a behaviour gap for iPad and iPhone browsers on Patterns' HTTPS remote. The fix is to set Life to 825 days and change the test that currently pins five years (Patterns/tests/Patterns.Core.Tests/ShowBus12Tests.cs:26). A renewal test already exists at :39-40.

(3) §9's "Claude" is not a breach of Stagewatch's rule. That rule is about authorship identifiers in pushed work, and Claude is the AI service Stagewatch and AGMessage actually call and name in their UI (SettingsDialog.xaml:529, CloudAdvisor.cs:35, AGMessage lib/ai.js). AGMessage's copy (line 156) matches the master. Patterns' "The language model" is an exception its own header declares (Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md:1). The wording change is optional.

(4) No tree has a test comparing its copy with the master. Adding one is new work, and it must allow Patterns' declared model-name exception.

title: The master contradicts itself and sets no limits
fix: Stagewatch master: proto 2 = 1.2 (or 'tls/approvals mark 1.2'), fix the tables, set limits (hello <= 2048 B, caps <= 32, context commands <= 256, items <= 64, context <= 64 KB), and say id is 6-40 [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Raise Stagewatch's caps cap to 32.
statement: The master contradicts itself and sets no limits. Its header says 1.2 is marked by hello `tls` and caps `approvals`. Its §2 table still defines proto only as "1 = 1.1 contract", and every node sends proto 1; Stagewatch's own record also calls proto the slide-feed version. §2's `t` list lacks `playmap`. Its ports list lacks `https`, `companion` and `sync`. Its caps list lacks `approvals` and most words the nodes actually send: Stagewatch's screens, aux, slides-in and copilot; AGMessage's action-prompts, documents and proposals; PlayMap's state, playlist, media, mapping, scan, show and video.*. The hello example has no `tls`. §4 uses `seq` for both a per-frame counter (Stagewatch's frame, PlayMap's STATE) and a per-clip discontinuity counter (Patterns' video.seq, PlayMap's clip.seq). §6 caps `recent` at 20 but sets no limit on items or commands. The master sets no hello byte, caps, `t` or `id` limit; only PlayMap's SHOWBUS-NODE.md writes any down. The readers differ: Stagewatch takes 2048 B, 16 caps, t up to 16 and id up to 40; Patterns 4096 B, 32 caps, t up to 32 and id up to 64; AGMessage 4096 B, 20 caps of up to 24 characters, and it drops `playmap` hellos; PlayMap 4096 B (its comment says 2048) and 16 caps. PlayMap sends exactly 16 caps, so any new PlayMap cap would be silently cut by Stagewatch and PlayMap's own reader. Stagewatch's node id is 12 hex; the spec says 8, which Patterns, AGMessage and PlayMap use. The proposed fix stands. It should also add `playmap` and `sync` to the §2 tables and rewrite the caps list from what the nodes actually send.

title: Stagewatch/docs/NODES.md describes the old links
fix: Stagewatch: rewrite NODES.md from the code (or fold it into SHOWBUS.md §8), and drop 9700 from Find once Patterns' 9928 hello is walked (Patterns L47).
statement:
Stagewatch/docs/NODES.md has not changed since 2.11.1 and describes links that have since changed.
(a) AGMessage: the doc says AGMessage listens on 9700, announces web:3023, passes its key as pin= and needs a control key. AGMessage now uses only 9928, announces ports.http, sends the key as an Authorization: Bearer header and asks for a node-scope key. The section also leaves out receipts, context and proposals.
(b) Patterns link: the doc says plain AUTH and a 7 s drop. The code does a NONCE/AUTH-PROOF exchange with an @hi probe, falls back to plain AUTH for old desks, and drops after 12 s.
(c) Hello: the id is persisted per install, not per run, and Stagewatch hears every kind.
The 250 ms to 5 s backoff, proto as the slide-feed version, and the top-level web field are not stale doc. NODES.md matches Stagewatch's code on all three, and that code differs from SHOWBUS.md §2 and §4 (backoff 0.5 s doubling to 5 s with jitter; proto is the Show Bus version). The fix for those is in code or code comments (PatternsLink.cs:189,229-230; RemoteSlides.cs:117), not only in NODES.md. Find listening on UDP 9700 (PatternsLink.cs:418-444) is likewise a code-versus-spec problem against SHOWBUS.md:45-46, and NODES.md:72,90 describe it correctly. It is fair to keep 9700 until Patterns' 9928 hello is walked (Patterns/docs/OPEN.md L47).

title: AGMessage's documented cadence and caps differ from its code and the contract
fix: AGMessage: ping every second tick (2 s) or update the doc. Spec: add 'proposes' to the vocabulary and rename AGMessage's cap to it.
statement: AGMessage's papers say the Stagewatch WS ping goes every 2 s (AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:10, AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:9). The code actually pings on every 1 s watch tick (nodes.js:221, 350-354). This is harmless: Stagewatch answers pings without any rate limit, and the contract sets no ping interval. The fix is to change the doc and the comment to 1 s, or to ping on every other tick. Separately, the caps list in Show Bus 1.2 (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:41, copied in AGMessage/docs and Patterns/docs at line 43) is stale for every node. It leaves out 1.2's own 'approvals', Stagewatch's screens/aux/slides-in/copilot, Patterns' video.*/state, and AGMessage's action-prompts/documents/proposals. No reader checks caps against a list, and desks are found by 'approvals' alone, so AGMessage's 'proposals' cap cannot be misread by any code. The fix is in the spec: list the caps the nodes actually send, including 'approvals', and say that unknown caps are ignored. Renaming AGMessage's cap to 'proposes' is optional, and if done it must also change AGMessage/app/test/tls.test.js:82. Value: low.

title: AGMessage confirms the TLS pin and shows 'connected' on a frame any client gets
fix: AGMessage: confirm the pin only after an authenticated 2xx (GET /api/context with the key), and show 'key refused' from that call. Stagewatch could also send {type:'auth',ok:false} on a refused key.
statement:
AGMessage shows 'connected' as soon as Stagewatch upgrades the WebSocket (nodes.js:323), before any frame arrives. It confirms the TLS pin on the first 'state' frame (nodes.js:329). Stagewatch upgrades every /ws request (WebServer.cs:1168) and reports the auth result only to role=control sockets (1216-1219). So with no viewing code set, a refused, missing or revoked key on AGMessage's non-control socket silently gets the same Public frame a valid key gets (1154-1164, 1015-1016, 1422). The link then reads 'connected' and pins the certificate on unauthenticated use, against AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:10 and Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:175.

When a viewing code is set, the pin is not confirmed. Stagewatch sends auth ok:false with view:true (1206), but AGMessage's 'Stagewatch refused' line is overwritten by 'reconnecting' on the close (nodes.js:343-344).

Fix:
- AGMessage: set 'connected' and confirm the pin only after an authenticated 2xx, for example the fetchContext GET /api/context already made at onopen. Turn a 401/403 from that call into a sticky 'key refused' status.
- Stagewatch: send {type:'auth',ok:false,error} for any supplied key it refuses, whatever the role, or refuse the upgrade with a 401.

title: No interop test runs real apps against each other
fix: Stagewatch's headless rig (tools/Stagewatch.Rig) plus a cross-repo job that starts the rig, PlayMap's engine (Linux), AGMessage (node) and a Patterns headless node, then asserts: hellos heard both ways, contexts posted, an approval to each target done, a stuck beat drops every follower, a VT link to PlayMap with a receipt.
evidence: Stagewatch/tests/Stagewatch.Tests/ShowBusTests.cs:226-289 (fake desk); Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Net.Tests/StagewatchLinkTests.cs:17-20 (FakeStagewatch); Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Net.Tests/WireServerTests.cs:64; AGMessage/app/test/tls.test.js:118; Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:37,40,43 (L47, L50, L56); Patterns/docs/QUALIFICATION.md:656-658,678-680; Stagewatch/docs/ECOSYSTEM.md:153-154
