statement:
No test, CI job or walk runs two real apps of the ecosystem against each other. Each Stagewatch interop test on either end plays the other side with a scripted peer:
- In Stagewatch: Patterns' desk (ShowBusTests.cs:226-289, Program.cs:1276).
- In PlayMap: Stagewatch (StagewatchLinkTests.cs:17-20, StagewatchSinkTests.cs:13), and a "Stagewatch-style" line client (WireServerTests.cs:64).
- In AGMessage: Stagewatch's desk (tls.test.js:91-118, resilience.test.js:235).
- In Patterns: Stagewatch (ShowBus12AppTests.cs:131).

The one test that uses another app's code is PlayMap checking its context against a copy of Patterns' Eye parser (PatternsEyeCopy.cs). It is not the running app, and it does not involve Stagewatch.

Untested end to end:
- Stagewatch's real PatternsLink against PlayMap's TCP 9941, which PlayMap's SHOWBUS-NODE.md:36 tells operators to use. Stagewatch's suite has no PlayMap hello or context at all.
- Stagewatch's real /api/proposals JSON as AGMessage's StagewatchLink reads it, and as PlayMap's sink reads it.
- Patterns' StagewatchLinkService against real Stagewatch frames and its approval queue.
- A peer's proposal of a window verb, which Stagewatch's context lists for peers, run through the real approval desk. No peer proposes window lines today; Stagewatch's Screens and windows send nothing to peers, so that direction does not exist rather than being untested.

Stagewatch's headless rig (tools/Stagewatch.Rig) has no Show Bus beacon, links or peers yet (Program.cs:296-300), so it would need them before a cross-repo job could use it. No conformance suite exists or is planned: ECOSYSTEM.md:153-154 is only a risk note. Patterns' walk rows for the link and for TLS and approvals (QUALIFICATION.md §26 and §27, OPEN.md L47, L50 and L56) are unwalked.

title: Patterns and PlayMap serve STATE and CONTEXT to unpaired wire peers
fix: Patterns and PlayMap: push STATE only after pairing (or to trusted or loopback peers), sending NONCE first. Stagewatch: read STATE after 'OK paired'. Or the spec names the open-STATE exemption explicitly.
evidence: Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:20; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ControlService.cs:356-363,501,763-774; Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:17-18,38-41 vs :591-592; Mapper/docs/WIRE.md ('A connection's life' items 2 and 4)
statement:
Show Bus §1.4 says show data travels only on authenticated links, but no node does this on its read paths, and the spec names no exemption.
- Patterns (deliberately, per Patterns/docs/PLAN.md §103.7 and REMOTE.md:38-41) greets every TCP wire connection with STATE before NONCE. It pushes STATE to every peer, paired or not, and answers all its queries, CONTEXT included, to unpaired peers. That STATE carries the show name, deck and device addresses, and web.url. Patterns' own REMOTE.md:591-592 contradicts this.
- PlayMap opens only its TCP line wire: NONCE comes first, then HELLO brings STATE pushes and STATE and CONTEXT answer as open queries. Its WebSocket line channel and its HTTP /api/state and /api/context already need pairing or the token.
- Stagewatch's only link to either node, PatternsLink, which also dials PlayMap on port 9941, pairs by AUTH-PROOF when it hears NONCE and accepts STATE at any time. It would keep working if STATE were pushed right after "OK paired". It depends on open STATE only when no token is set on its side.
- Stagewatch's own /ws frames, viewer pages and Companion TCP 9923 also serve show state without authentication.
The fix: either amend §1.4 and §7 to name the open-read tier (reads open on line wires and /ws, show data never in beacons), or have Patterns hold its greeting STATE until pairing on a token-protected desk and then push it after "OK paired", as PlayMap's WebSocket channel already does, and do the same for PlayMap's TCP wire. The G09 window-address concern applies through Patterns' STATE web.url, but only if a window address is ever put on air.

title: Opportunity: let a Stagewatch window show a heard peer's page
fix: Stagewatch: content 'node:<id>/<path>' resolved to a heard node's https address with a pin, allowed only for nodes whose context lists the page as public, and a per-window CSP frame-src for that origin. High risk in the copilot.
statement:
A Stagewatch window can show only Stagewatch's own pages, and it blocks foreign content at three points:
- ValidPath and CanShow refuse any address that is not a path on this Stagewatch (AppSettings.cs:305-308, ScreenWindows.cs:125-159).
- The window CSP allows frames only from Stagewatch itself (frame-src 'self', WebServer.cs:621).
- The window shell fails any page that lacks `window.SW`, and every cross-origin page lacks it as far as the shell can tell (window.js:87-91).

The peers have little a window could carry anyway:
- **PlayMap** serves no viewable page. /fleet and /health are JSON (FleetWebModules.cs:51-58, 195). Its only HTML pages are /tls and the /scan phone pages, which send frame-ancestors 'none'.
- **Patterns** does not forbid framing, and its /multiview page could be framed. But once a pairing token is set, the picture it loads (/mv.jpg) is refused, because its SameSite=Strict token cookie never reaches a cross-site frame.
- **AGMessage** forbids framing (frame-ancestors 'self').

The proposed fix would need more than the claim lists:
- the window.js SW check relaxed for named origins;
- a per-window frame-src;
- the TV's browser trusting the peer's self-signed certificate at the operating-system level, since Stagewatch's app-to-app pin cannot apply inside a browser frame;
- a new "public pages" field in the Show Bus context, which does not exist today;
- for PlayMap, an HTML board page that can be framed.

The lower-risk alternative is a page of Stagewatch's own that draws heard peers' context and fleet data. Stagewatch already receives peer context via POST /api/peers/context. That keeps the window same-origin with no CSP or pinning change. Value: low.

title: PlayMap cannot render a web page, yet imports one as 'added'
fix: PlayMap: refuse MEDIA IMPORT of a page with the reason ('pages need a browser source — not built; use NDI from a browser, or LINK STAGEWATCH … WINDOW', see G11) until a renderer exists. Never keep a /w/ URL in the project.
statement: PlayMap has no web renderer: MediaBackend.Open returns null for MediaKind.Web (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/MediaBackend.cs:144-145), and no browser package is referenced. Even so, MEDIA IMPORT of any http(s) URL that is not YouTube adds a Web item and answers "added <name>" (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/EngineCore.Content.cs:395-406). PlayMap then reports the item as fine. Readiness says Present and Verified, "read from the network when it plays" (MediaBackend.cs:381-382). MEDIA LIST says ready:true and state "ready" (EngineCore.Content.cs:508-510, 527-528). MEDIA FETCH says the item "is rendered from its address" (EngineCore.Content.cs:447). If a person or the assistant pastes a Stagewatch window address (http(s)://<pc>:9924/w/<token>), PlayMap plays nothing while showing the item as ready. If no name is given, the item is named after the full URL (EngineCore.Content.cs:393), so the window's pass is kept in the project as both location and name and appears in the edit label and the "added" reply. No sender does this automatically. No Stagewatch, Show Bus or AGMessage code sends MEDIA IMPORT. The window:<name> context item carries no address (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ScreenWindows.cs:345). Stagewatch/docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:99-100 records that PlayMap does not yet take a window address. A side effect: any https stream, HLS included, is filed as Web, so it does not play either. The fix should refuse a page import with the reason and keep the address out of the name, the reply and the project. It should also correct readiness, MEDIA LIST and MEDIA FETCH for Web items, and file https HLS URLs as Stream.

title: Stagewatch's VT transport fails on Patterns' playlist items and stingers
fix: Patterns: close L48 and L49 (transport for playlist items, VIDEO … ON <key>). Stagewatch: once Patterns lists the key in STATE.video.key, send ON <key>.
statement:
Patterns refuses VIDEO PAUSE and VIDEO STOP when the clip on air is a playlist item or a stinger's clip (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ShowActions.Content.cs:481,486,501; L48 in Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:38). PLAY on such a clip is refused as "already playing". SEEK, END and RESTART work on it.

Patterns already publishes the clip's role and key in STATE.video: `role` at Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/CommandRouter.cs:237, `tag` ("PLAYLIST" / "STINGER CLIP") at :238 and `key` at :252. Stagewatch's TryParseState ignores them (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:386-414).

Stagewatch's Transport() check (PatternsLink.cs:148-154) never looks at the role, so `patterns pause` and `patterns stop` are always sent:
- The HTTP, WebSocket or Companion caller gets a receipt with stage "accepted", not a refusal (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:87; MainViewModel.Receipts.cs:38).
- The journal records "Patterns clip paused" / "Patterns clip stopped at the top" as if it had happened (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:88).
- Patterns' "ERR @id" reaches only StatusLine (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:65-66).

Fix:
- Stagewatch, now and with no Patterns change: parse STATE.video.role. In Transport(), refuse pause and stop for "playlist" or "stinger" with Patterns' own reason, pointing to `patterns end`, `patterns restart` or `patterns seek`, so the caller's receipt says "refused". Journal only once Patterns' OK receipt has arrived.
- Patterns: L48 (a pause that also holds the playlist sequencer's clock and the stinger's ending) is the real cure.
- L49 (VIDEO … ON <key>) is not needed here. Stagewatch drives only the clip on air, and a key would not avoid the refusal, which is decided by the clip's role.

title: Stagewatch's ECOSYSTEM roadmap: manifest, merged journal and one preflight not built
fix: Stagewatch: a 'Link all' flow that mints a node key per heard node and hands it over the pinned TLS hello path after an operator click on each node. A preflight that reads every peer's context and reds. A merged report from peers' 'recent'.
statement: Stagewatch has no network-wide readiness gate, merged report or one-click linking. (1) Linking: an operator mints a node key per peer in Settings → Remote → New key… and types it into Patterns, PlayMap and AGMessage, and types Patterns' pairing token back into Stagewatch. No exchange is approved per node, and no key goes over a pinned TLS link. Stagewatch has no PlayMap link of its own, apart from what PlayMap posts. (2) Preflight: Producer → Show network and PeerAdvice already show every heard node's light and its red/amber problems. But it is a passive dashboard. It relies on peers posting their context, checks clock offset only against Patterns, never checks keys, pins or screens across nodes, and never shows "ready for doors". PlayMap's preflight and Patterns' Super Check each cover only their own node. (3) Report: /report and /api/report.csv are built from Stagewatch's own journal only. Peers' `recent` lines are already held in PeerContexts but never merged in. The report's AI section also drops notes on peer proposals sent to the shared queue (the prefixes don't match AiPrefixes), which breaks SHOWBUS §11. (4) The `/.well-known/show-node.json` manifest is not a gap in the contract. Show Bus 1.2 replaced it with the hello's caps and ports and the context's `commands` with risk. Only ECOSYSTEM.md's stale roadmap needs updating, or the gap is narrowed to the unpublished key scope per route.
